# Linux ARM64 / Raspberry Pi

InBharat Audio supports a production Linux ARM64 build for Pocket AI Pi while keeping the core reusable. The shipping build excludes deterministic ASR/TTS fixtures and experimental research modules.

Build natively on a 64-bit Raspberry Pi or cross-build with an AArch64 GNU toolchain:

```sh
./scripts/build_linux_arm64.sh
```

The script refuses to call the output valid unless `file` identifies an AArch64 binary and the production registry contains no `reference-asr`, `reference-tts`, or deferred KWS engines.

Real ASR/TTS are provided by a separately verified `audiocpp_cli` plus real model packages. A build succeeding without those assets is **not** proof of speech functionality. Pocket AI release requires the real end-to-end speech acceptance attestation generated by the product acceptance runner.

For Raspberry Pi, start CPU-first. Vulkan is allowed only after the selected Pi/driver image and exact speech model pass latency, memory, thermal, and output-parity tests on physical hardware.
